Featured Arizona examples include Mesa Public Schools, Chandler Unified School District, Tucson Unified School District, Peoria Unified School District, and Gilbert Public Schools, with district-specific details such as two-hour early releases, professional learning days, intersessions, teacher inservice/workdays, modified Wednesdays, grade-band early dismissals, K-6 conference half days, and approved calendar PDFs.
about:
Arizona public school calendars are approved locally by district. Large districts often begin in July or early August and finish in May, with fall, winter, and spring breaks arranged around grading periods, professional learning days, and early-release schedules.

Featured Arizona examples include Mesa Public Schools, Chandler Unified School District, Tucson Unified School District, Peoria Unified School District, and Gilbert Public Schools. Mesa uses frequent two-hour early releases, professional learning days, semester exam early releases, and grading-period checkpoints. Chandler Unified uses an intersession calendar with 180 student days, 190 teacher days, teacher inservice/workdays, and junior high or high school early-dismissal notes. Tucson Unified uses weekly Wednesday early release, conference half-days, Rodeo Break, and separate staff days. Peoria Unified uses modified Wednesday early releases, elementary conference dates, high school early-release dates, furlough/no-school dates, teacher workdays, and rotation-calendar resources. Gilbert Public Schools publishes multi-year family calendar PDFs with one-hour early releases, K-12 half days, K-6 conference half days, semester day counts, grading days, and summer school windows.

Families should treat the districtwide calendar as the starting point, then check the assigned school for bell schedules, transportation notices, testing, athletics, performances, graduation details, rotation schedules, and campus-specific events.

planningTips: Do not assume Arizona districts start after Labor Day; many begin in July or early August.
Check whether an early release applies to all students, only elementary students, junior high students, or high school students.
Teacher inservice, professional learning, and workdays are not regular student attendance days.
Families comparing Phoenix-area districts should verify fall break and intersession weeks separately because nearby districts do not always align.
commonHolidaysDescription: Arizona districts commonly list Labor Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving, winter break, Presidents Day, spring break, and Memorial Day, but intersession labels and exact dates vary by district.

faqs.q: When do Arizona schools usually start?
faqs.a: Arizona school start dates vary by district, but many large districts begin in July or early August. Families should select their district calendar to confirm the official first day.

faqs.q: Are Arizona school calendars the same statewide?
faqs.a: No. Arizona school calendars are approved locally by district, so start dates, breaks, intersessions, professional learning days, and early-release rules can differ.

faqs.q: What are intersessions on Arizona school calendars?
faqs.a: Some Arizona districts use intersessions as longer breaks after grading periods. Chandler Unified, for example, lists first, second, and third intersessions.

faqs.q: Do Arizona districts use early-release days?
faqs.a: Yes, but the pattern varies. Some districts use weekly early releases; others list early dismissal by grade band, conference period, exam window, or campus group.

faqs.q: Can I add an Arizona school calendar to Google Calendar?
faqs.a: Yes. District pages on MySchoolDates include calendar download options when available, including ICS files that can be imported into Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook.
